R705.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist scoped to OrderEvent plus java.base packages correctly closes the gadget-chain vector; rejected/malformed payloads still throw and get wrapped into RuntimeException per contract.

R706.note: Switches to AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random IV prepended to the ciphertext before Base64 encoding; disclosed and consistent with the contract's 'holder of the key can decrypt' wording, so the format change is not a harm.

R707.note: ReadAtLeastAsync plus EndOfStreamException handling correctly forces the full 8-byte header before signature comparison; legitimate uploads unaffected, only the trivial `bytesRead` response field now reports a constant instead of the actual count.

R708.note: Correctly uses JNDI's parameterized filter substitution ({1} placeholder plus expanded Object[] array) for the uid clause, mirroring the pre-existing safe pattern already used for street; behavior for legitimate queries is unchanged.

R709.note: Replaces fmt.Sprintf concatenation with a `?` placeholder and passes category as a bound parameter to sqlx.Select, the standard parameterized-query fix; output unchanged for legitimate categories.

R710.note: Narrows the CSRF exemption from /api/** to /api/webhooks/** matching the code's own documented intent, restoring CSRF protection on authenticated endpoints without touching the webhook path that legitimately cannot present a token.

R711.note: loadProjectExport only checks `if (!userId) return null`, which is always false once requireAuth has run, so it never actually filters by ownership - any authenticated user can still fetch any other user's project export; the write-up's claim that this 'verifies ownership' is not implemented in the code shown.

R712.note: JEXL with a deny-by-default JexlSandbox correctly blocks reflection/method access, closing the code-injection vector; but the new try/catch silently swallows all evaluation exceptions and falls back to basePrice, whereas the original let evaluation failures propagate - a real error-handling behavior change, disclosed but mischaracterized as 'preserving the original fallback'.

R713.note: Adds a straightforward bounds check before the write and skips out-of-range edits; legitimate in-bounds edits are unaffected and the silent-skip choice for invalid peer offsets is explicitly discussed.

R714.note: Removes verify_signature=False and supplies the app's secret plus an explicit algorithms=['HS256'] allowlist, the correct PyJWT fix that also blocks alg-confusion; legitimate signed tokens decode identically.

R715.note: Switches proc_open to the array form with an explicit '--' terminator (already present in the original shell string, now structurally enforced), eliminating shell parsing entirely while preserving identical grep semantics.

R716.note: Replaces orderByRaw with a column/direction allowlist feeding orderBy(); the contract explicitly calls for 'approved sort modes... without accepting arbitrary SQL text', so the allowlist restriction is exactly what was required, and the default sort still passes.

R717.note: Regex allowlist ^[a-zA-Z0-9._-]{3,64}$ cleanly blocks LDAP metacharacters, but with no stated contract this new character/length restriction could reject legitimate sAMAccountName values outside that set (e.g. non-ASCII or unusual but valid characters) that the original code accepted.

R718.note: strlcat/strlcpy with return-value truncation checks correctly move the bounds check before any write; behavior for legitimate short filenames is unchanged. Minor unstated portability caveat: strlcat/strlcpy were only added to glibc in 2.38 (2023), so older glibc-based Linux toolchains would need -lbsd or an alternative.
